subject: Post-call: Argos data ops incident handling & break-glass plan
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Sophia Ramos <sophia.ramos@argosbank.com>, David Lin <david.lin@argosbank.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 25 Apr 2027 15:05:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Argos data ops incident handling & break-glass plan

Hi Sophia / David —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum: you had good questions around PII handling, retention, and how support would access data in an incident. Below are the items we agreed to follow up on from the call: 

1) PII categories and examples you want redacted or tokenized (e.g., SSN, account numbers, postal address). Please confirm the full list and any downstream analytic uses that would still need those fields.

2) Data retention windows by data type (chat logs, ephemeral KV cache, full request/response archives). You mentioned a 30/90/365 model for most assets — can you confirm which classes map to which window?

3) Logging and audit requirements — examples you requested: sample access log entries, retention of audit trails, and how long break-glass justifications are stored.

4) Support access controls (RBAC) and break-glass flow — we proposed:
   - scoped support roles with JIT elevation that requires two-step approval
   - break-glass events trigger immediate audit, email to your security contacts, and immutable justification stored with the session

5) Residency and export controls — confirm whether any production inference must remain in us-east-1 only, and whether we need encryption-in-transit plus bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for certain datasets.

Next steps (proposed timeline):
- We’ll send a draft access matrix and a short break-glass playbook by EOD Monday (attached: argos-data-access-matrix.xlsx).
- You’ll iterate on PII categories and retention mapping; aim to send back comments by Wed 28 Apr.
- We’ll produce an example audit log export and a diagram of the support JIT flow by Fri 30 Apr.

Attachments: argos-data-access-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet — columns: data_class, pii_flag, retention_days, support_role_allowed, justification_required)

If this looks right I’ll loop in Marissa from Solutions to draft a short SOC/controls summary you can include in your procurement packet.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov

Subject: Re: Post-call: Argos data ops incident handling & break-glass plan

Thanks Olga — that recap is very helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- PII categories: please include SSN, PAN/account numbers, full name + DOB combination, and customer contact info. We can provide a spreadsheet if that helps.

- Retention: we want transaction-level logs for 365 days, chat transcripts for 90 days, and KV caches only 30 days unless explicitly persisted. Can you confirm how Redwood separates ephemeral KV cache from persisted logs?

- Break-glass: we require that any elevated session stores the justification and approver identity for 2 years and that logs are tamper-evident. Can you provide a sample audit entry?

We also need a short one-page controls summary for procurement (inc. encryption at rest, KMS options) — we’d like that attached when you send materials to procurement@argosbank.com.

Best,
Sophia
Sophia Ramos
Head of Data Ops, Argos Bank
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Post-call: Argos data ops incident handling & break-glass plan

Olga — forwarding notes for the internal plan. Key technical responses to Sophia’s asks below (draft):

- KV cache vs persisted logs: our runtime keeps a short-lived KV cache in-GPU/memory that is never written to persistent storage unless the customer explicitly enables session persistence for debugging. We can enforce a 30-day TTL on any persisted cache artifacts and provide a separate retention bucket for archived logs.

- Sample audit entry (example):
   timestamp: 2027-04-26T18:07:34Z
   user: support_jit@support.redwood.ai
   action: elevate_session
   target_session_id: sess-0a12b3c4
   justification: "customer reported PII exposure, elevated to inspect headers"
   approver: security-lead@argosbank.com
   immutable_hash: sha256:3a7b...

- RBAC recommendation: three-tier roles — support_readonly, support_jit, support_admin. support_jit requires an approval token from the customer's security contact and expires after 1 hour. All elevations log both the approver and the reason; justification is stored immutable with an HMAC and retained for 730 days.

- Break-glass process: we propose a canary approach for production:
   1) Support requests access and provides incident ticket link (required).
   2) Customer security approves via SSO/approval service (email first pass allowed for pilot).
   3) Elevated access is granted in-scoped (resource-limited) for up to 1 hour with automatic revocation.
   4) System captures a tamper-evident justification artefact and sends a copy to customer-sre@argosbank.com

Links: internal playbook draft https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/argos-breakglass-playbook (draft)

Marissa — can you add the short one-pager for procurement (encryption options/BYOK + SOC 2 highlights)? I’ll tidy the sample audit entry.

Thanks,
Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Product Security Engineer

- Retention mapping: we’ve modeled transaction logs = 365, chat transcripts = 90, persisted debug artifacts (only if enabled) = 30. Ephemeral KV cache is never persisted by default.

- Audit example: see Karthik’s sample entry above — we’ll include a downloadable CSV of anonymized sample logs when we share the procurement packet.

- Controls summary for procurement: Marissa attached the one-pager with encryption-at-rest options (BYOK via KMS) and SOC 2 references. Procurement: if you want a customized export of controls for your packet, reply-all and we’ll prepare a DocuSign + controls bundle.
